charge_behavior.notes: Samsung advertises 25W wired charging (25W-class phone; no 45W SFC 2.0 tier). Full speed requires a PD 3.0 PPS source covering 3.3-11V at >=2.75A (Samsung Super Fast Charging). Metered with multiple PPS chargers (45W/65W/100W/140W): the phone converges at ~9V/2.5A = 21.6-22.9W, so any 25W+ PPS port reaches full speed and bigger bricks gain nothing. One independent bench measured 22.9W from a plain non-PPS 9V PD charger too, but Samsung/GSMArena guidance says PPS is required - the matcher models the PPS path. Measured charge times (GSMArena, 25W PPS): 28% in 15 min, 53% in 30 min, full in 1h27m.

soc_curves.note: Segment watts derived from milestone deltas; approximate.

pps.note: SFC 25W operating point measured at ~9V/2.5A (21.6-22.9W). Source PPS must cover 3.3-11V at >=2.75A.

charge_behavior.notes: Correction from earlier repo data: the real ceiling is ~29-30W, not 20W. The iPad negotiates a 15V fixed PDO and peaks at 30.06W (15V/2A) with a 67W charger, 29.1W with 35W, 28.9W with 29W - but only 19.6W from the bundled 20W adapter, which is locked to the 9V PDO. The cap is the negotiated PDO, not a hard 20W limit. Higher-watt chargers beyond ~30W save nothing on total time (~2h14-2h32 full depending on charger). Measured 0-100% on the bundled 20W charger ~2h32.

charge_behavior.notes: Apple specifies fast charging with a 96W or higher source, but the laptop does not draw 96W from anything: metered ceiling is ~88-92W (Apple 140W charger = 91.8W, Anker 100W = 87.8W, CUKTECH 210Wh bank = 88.9W), all at 20V/~4.5A. So a 90W+ source (Anker 747, Y270, CUKTECH 10 on a good cable) reaches essentially full speed. MagSafe 3 and USB-C charge identically. Measured 0-100%: ~93 min on 96W, 107 min on 70W. Under full system load (75-98W draw) the adapter is saturated and battery charging slows or pauses.

charge_curves.reference: PhoneArena in-box EP-OL300 puck: 45% @30min, 70% @45min, full 1h19m (40mm); reviewers report 80-115 min depending on model
charge_curves.note: Estimated taper - puck is a flat 5V/2A source until the watch slows above ~70-80%.

charge_behavior.notes: Official puck is Samsung EP-OL300: USB-C input rated 5V/2A (10W), requiring a PD adapter with at least 5V/2A. The puck has a PD-certified chip but only draws 5V. A higher-watt brick does not speed it up - the puck is the bottleneck; any arsenal USB-C port (all support 5V/3A+) runs it at full speed. Samsung warns non-PD sources, some power banks, and multi-port hubs can slow charging. Measured full charge ~1h19m-1h54m depending on reviewer and model; 45% in 30 min. The watch has no USB-C port; the model tracks the puck input. No reverse PowerShare support. Efficiency set to 0.15: measured 45% in 30 min on a 10W puck implies ~1.5W into the battery - the wireless transfer and watch-side regulation dominate, so the puck input wattage overstates charging speed.
